_comment: Real numbers reported this session from the user's own Mac Mini benchmarks + powermetrics, not fabricated placeholders. GPU/SME entries are Promise.all()-concurrent (2 simultaneous matmuls), NOT solo peak -- both backends converged on the same ~5.5 GFLOPS ceiling under concurrency, which is itself evidence the bottleneck may be shared/upstream (dispatch overhead, memory bandwidth) rather than either compute unit's real peak. Only ANE has a measured watts figure (via powermetrics); AMX/BLAS/VNNI/GPU/SME watts are not yet measured on this machine -- do not synthesize them.

ANE.measuredVia: real matmul benchmark, validated against actual math outputs (not just timing) before trusting the numbers
ANE.note: power draw is nearly flat (~11W) across all three shapes -- the GFLOPS/W swing is a utilization/shape-tiling curve, not a power curve. Not yet integrated into the user's CPE benchmark harness; VNNI (below) took significant optimization work to reach its measured ~40x-over-baseline figure, used as the expectation-setting reference for what ANE integration will likely need too, rather than a naive throughput-ratio extrapolation.

AMX-BF16.note: Apple's own undocumented CPU-integrated matrix coprocessor (reverse-engineered instruction set, unrelated to Intel's AMX-TILE ISA extension of the same name), bf16 mode

AMX-INT8.note: same Apple AMX coprocessor, int8 mode -- consistently ~2-2.2x AMX-BF16 at matching shapes, the expected ratio for double the elements/cycle at half the bit width

BLAS-fp32.note: OpenBLAS-style fp32 path, no tile/dot-product acceleration

VNNI.note: user's shorthand for the ARM SDOT/NEON int8 dot-product path (no literal Intel VNNI silicon on Apple Silicon). Took substantial optimization work to reach these numbers from an initially slow baseline -- these are NOT naive/out-of-the-box figures.

GPU.note: 2 concurrent GPU matmuls via Promise.all() -- this is NOT solo-GPU peak throughput, it's the observed average under 2x concurrency

SME.note: machine has 2 SME units; 2 concurrent matmuls via Promise.all() landed on the exact same ~5.5 GFLOPS as the GPU entry above -- worth re-testing both at solo (non-concurrent) throughput before trusting either as a real per-unit peak, since two structurally different backends converging on an identical number under concurrency suggests a shared bottleneck (dispatch/scheduling overhead or memory bandwidth), not a coincidence in real per-unit capability.
